content: Internal Revenue Service, Special Revenue Officer Daniel Carter, badge ID 624573. With whom am I speaking today?
This is Margaret Ellis. I got a message about some kind of urgent tax issue?

Yes, Ms. Ellis, thank you for verifying. I have your file under case number TXF-0039281. Our system has detected anomalies in your federal tax filings for fiscal years 2018 to 2022. Are you aware of any such discrepancies?
No, I always file my taxes with the help of my son. I don't understand, what kind of anomalies?

According to Form 1040 audits and cross-referencing with 1099s and SSA-1098s, there is a significant underreporting of income totaling $3,214.67, triggering a Federal Tax Fraud Alert under Section 7201. This is a very serious matter.
Oh my goodness, that can't be right. I just have Social Security and a small pension. I can't believe I did anything wrong.

Ms. Ellis, as an IRS Revenue Officer, I must inform you that due to these discrepancies, the system has already generated a non-bailable arrest warrant under your name. This is not a courtesy call; legal action is already in the works.
A warrant? For me? I don't even drive, let alone break laws. What does this mean?

The implications are severe. You are facing federal charges for tax evasion. If the warrant is enforced, your Social Security benefits will be frozen, your bank accounts seized, and you could be remanded to federal custody by the local sheriff's office as early as this afternoon.
No, please, I can't lose my benefits. I depend on every dollar to survive. Isn't there some way to fix this? I never meant to do anything wrong.

There is a protocol called an 'Alternative Resolution Settlement,' which allows first-time offenders to resolve the issue before escalation. However, it must be initiated before the warrant reaches active enforcement status in our system.
What do I have to do? I can't go to jail, and I can't lose my money.

To initiate the Alternative Resolution, the IRS requires a provisional payment of the outstanding balance via a traceable transaction. Because your case is flagged as high-risk for immediate asset seizure, only IRS-approved payment methods will be accepted. These include certified wire transfer, Bitcoin payment, or authorized gift cards. Do you understand?
I think so, but I don't know how to do any of that. I don't use computers, and I don't have much in the bank.

No problem, Ms. Ellis. For seniors on fixed incomes, the IRS allows settlement via retail-certified gift cards, such as Apple, Google Play, or Target cards. You will need to visit a nearby store, acquire $1,500 in certified gift cards, and relay the codes for immediate processing. This will suspend the warrant.
Gift cards? That seems odd. Are you sure that's what the IRS wants?

Yes, ma'am. For flagged high-risk accounts, this is the only expedited, trackable method we can use to validate your intent to resolve the matter and put a hold on the legal action. Please do not share this with anyone at the store, as this is a confidential federal investigation.
Alright, I'll try to get to the store soon. What do I do once I have the cards?

Once you purchase the gift cards, stay on the line and scratch off the security strip on the cards. Read me each code. I will log them directly into the IRS payment portal under your case, TXF-0039281. This will generate an immediate suspension receipt.
Okay, I'll go now. Please promise me I won't lose my benefits if I do this.

As long as you comply and provide the required payment codes within the next 45 minutes, your Social Security and pension accounts will remain active, and the arrest warrant will be annulled. Failure to comply will result in irreversible enforcement.
I understand. I'll try to hurry. I just need to get my coat and walk to the pharmacy.
